thread:
samir (support): Hey team — escalating a private/VPC customer issue (Acme Payment). They're seeing intermittent 429s + latency spikes during client-side bursts. They run Redwood Private behind a customer-managed gateway (k8s nginx ingress + cloud LB). Customer reports that bursts >500 rps trigger 429s and lots of retries, which then blew past their quota and caused a billing alert. Need triage + repro steps.

emily (acme-corp): FYI logs from our gateway:  
```
2026-03-12T15:04:02Z GET /v1/generate 502 ms 429 "Too Many Requests" x-forwarded-for: 10.10.2.34
2026-03-12T15:04:03Z GET /v1/generate 498 ms 200
2026-03-12T15:04:04Z GET /v1/generate 120 ms 429
```
We're seeing `X-RateLimit-*` headers from Redwood for some 429s, but not consistently. Also note our ingress sets `limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=req_zone:10m rate=100r/s` and `limit_req zone=req_zone burst=200 nodelay`. Could that interact poorly with Redwood's backend?

jess (sre): Thanks. Key things to check: 1) where is rate limiting applied — client -> customer gateway vs gateway -> redwood? 2) Are source IPs preserved? If the gateway is using the LB's source IP or proxy-protocol incorrectly, upstream will see the same source and rate-limit by gateway IP. That will cause early 429s even though unique clients exist.

maria (eng-infra): Also watch for connection reuse / keepalives. If the customer LB SNATs connections, you can exhaust ephemeral ports or hit conntrack limits which causes accept latency and apparent throttling. Please paste `ss -s` and `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` if possible.

emily (acme-corp): Attaching quick repro script we used to simulate bursts:  
```
# small burst script (bash)
for i in {1..600}; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" "https://private-gateway.acme/v1/generate?prompt=hi" &
  if (( i % 50 == 0 )); then sleep 0.2; fi
done
wait
```
This produces ~200 429s in <60s.

samir (support): Repro works locally for me too against a test cluster. Observed headers: `X-RateLimit-Limit: 60000` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 59900` on some responses, but on others Redwood returns `Retry-After: 1` and `X-RateLimit-Policy: per_token` vs `per_ip`. Looks like mixed enforcement.

jess (sre): Two likely contributing factors: 1) customer-side ingress/nginx is applying its own per-ip token bucket (your `limit_req_zone`), 2) the gateway may be bundling requests over a small set of source IPs towards Redwood (NAT), and Redwood's per-IP or per-token quota triggers/or fallback policies kick in. If gateways normalize the client token header (Authorization) or share service account tokens across many clients, that can hit token-level quotas too.

emily (acme-corp): We do terminate TLS at the LB and pass traffic to nginx with proxy-protocol enabled. We also have a small pool of egress IPs for SNAT. We do preserve `X-Forwarded-For` though.

maria (eng-infra): Actionable checklist (suggested):
- Verify LB preserves client source IP to the ingress pod (or enable proxy-protocol end-to-end). If not possible, configure nginx to rate-limit by header (e.g., `$http_x_forwarded_for`), but be careful — `X-Forwarded-For` can be spoofed by clients unless LB strips it.
- Consider switching `limit_req_zone` key from `$binary_remote_addr` to `$http_x_real_ip` or a token header if you want per-client limits behind NAT: `limit_req_zone $http_x_forwarded_for zone=req:10m rate=100r/s;`
- Increase `burst` and `nodelay` temporarily to accommodate spikes, or enable a leaky-bucket smoothing in the gateway rather than strict reject.
- Check kube-proxy / conntrack: `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` and `sysctl net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range`. If conntrack drops are high, increase `nf_conntrack_max` and `nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established`.

jess (sre): From Redwood side: we have per-token quotas and per-customer fallback rules. If we see a high rate from one token, Redwood returns 429 with `X-RateLimit-Scope: token`. If we see high request rates from a single IP that violate our network-level protection we may return 429 with `X-RateLimit-Scope: ip`. We also have a short burst allowance; sustained bursts cause deterministic rejects.

samir (support): Emily — can you paste a raw failed request/response pair (headers included)? Need to see `Authorization`, `X-Forwarded-For`, `Host`, `Via` and any `X-Request-Id`. Also confirm whether you use a shared API key (server-side) vs per-client keys.

emily (acme-corp): Here's one sanitized example:  
```
> Request headers:
Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-*****
Host: private-gateway.acme
X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.45, 10.10.2.34
User-Agent: acme-payments/1.2

< Response headers:
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 1
X-RateLimit-Scope: token
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
```
We are definitely using a single backend API key for our service (server-side).

maria (eng-infra): That explains the `token` scope: Redwood is rate-limiting the API key. Two paths: 1) Redwood customers can enable per-client keys (issue per-customer tokens) so token-level throttling is distributed; 2) throttle/shape at the gateway by client id to avoid exhausting the single token.

jess (sre): Quick mitigation suggestions for customer until longer fix:
- Implement request queuing at the ingress (increase `burst` or use `limit_conn` to queue/smooth)\- Use per-client tokens (rotate the single token into short-lived, per-session tokens)\- Configure retry backoff on client side (exponential with jitter) so bursts don't amplify.

samir (support): Also note the billing impact: retries produce extra billed tokens. If the customer needs a billing credit while they remediate, open a formal billing ticket with the billing team and attach these logs. Tagging billing: @billing-team.

emily (acme-corp): We can do a quick change: switch nginx `limit_req_zone` to use `$http_x_forwarded_for` and increase `burst` to 400. We'll test in staging and report back. Also we'll consider per-session tokens.

maria (eng-infra): Please also run this conntrack check:  
```
# check conntrack counters
sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count
sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
# if count ~= max, increase it
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288
```
and inspect `kubectl logs` for nginx `limit_req` warnings.

jess (sre): From our logging side I'll look for clustering of `client_ip` or `token` in the 429s window and send a short report. If we see most 429s as `X-RateLimit-Scope: ip` vs `token`, that'll point to NAT/ingress problems.

samir (support): Action items: 
- emily: apply nginx temp change to staging (use XFF key + burst=400), run the burst script and paste results (due EOD).
- jess: produce 24h histogram of 429s by scope & source (T+2h).
- maria: document recommended nginx annotations and example `limit_req` config for our support KB (I'll stub a draft).
- samir: open billing escalation if customer asks for credit and add logs.

emily (acme-corp): Test results: staging with `limit_req_zone $http_x_forwarded_for ... burst=400` reduced 429s by ~90% for the same script. Only ~18 429s vs 200. We'll try per-session tokens next week. Thanks all. :tada: 

redwood-deploy-bot: deploy completed: private-gateway-config v1.3 -> applied to customer-staging (2026-03-12T17:01:05Z)

jess (sre): I'll post the Redwood-side analysis after the 2h window. Likely follow-ups: add KB entry on "Private/VPC: common causes of 429s behind customer gateways" and a sample nginx config.
